clauses.title: General Requirements
clauses.heading_line: 1.    General Requirements

fragments.text:
1.    General Requirements

           (a) Contract Package – P1: “Partial and Full Demolition/Dismantling of Buildings/Structures
               identified from JP Nagar 4th Phase Station to Mysore Road Station (from Ch: (-) 0.330
        Km to Ch: 10.550 Km) in Corridor-1of Bangalore Metro Rail Project Phase-3.”

          To  commence  the   civil   construction  works  and   float  the    civil   tenders,
              demolition/dismantling of the buildings and structures identified for the viaduct, double-
            decker structure, stations, loops, and ramps shall be undertaken.

             This package includes the demolition/dismantling of various types of commercial and
               residential buildings ranging from Basements, Ground Floor (G+0) to Ground +4 (G+4),
            as well as sheds. The scope of work includes demolition of the identified structures,
             salvage of specified items and materials, and removal and disposal of the resulting debris,
              walls with all leads and lifts, etc. The debris shall be disposed of at BBMP/GBA identified
         C&D waste management facility.

           The identified buildings and structures have been classified into the following categories:

              1.  Partial demolition/dismantling of all types of structures of varying heights, consisting of
              basements, ground floor and/or one or more upper floors (RCC framed structures,
                load-bearing structures with RCC roofs, and other structures such as AC roof
                  structures, etc.), by mechanical and manual methods, comprising cement concrete,
               stone masonry,  brickwork, steelwork, woodwork,  etc.,  with a  total quantity as
              mentioned in the BoQ.


              2.  Full demolition/dismantling of all types of structures of varying heights, consisting of
              basement level, ground floor and/or one or more upper floors (RCC framed structures,
                load-bearing structures with RCC roofs, and other structures such as AC roof
                  structures,  etc.), by mechanical and manual methods, with a  total quantity as
              mentioned in the BoQ.


              3.  Demolition/dismantling of compound walls of all shapes and heights by mechanical
             and manual methods, comprising cement concrete, stone masonry, brickwork,
                 steelwork, fencing, stone slab walls, chain-link fencing, etc., with a total quantity as
              mentioned in the BoQ.


              4.  Demolition/dismantling of steel structures such as bus stops, median grills, compound
                 wall grills, signboards, hoardings, etc., with a total quantity as mentioned in the BoQ.
                Dismantled/released material to be handed over to the concerned authority at the
                 locations specified by owning authority and removal of resulting debris with all lead
             and lifts and as directed by the Engineer.


           (b) Demolition and dismantling works.
           The work includes demolition, salvage of identified items and materials, and removal of
               resulting debris.  Debris shall be removed from the premises daily, unless otherwise
              directed, to avoid accumulation at the demolition premises.  The demolition shall be
              carried out after taking necessary strengthening methods for the buildings proposed for
              demolition and also for neighboring buildings. The contractor shall develop and take
            necessary strengthening methods for the balance portion of the structure not being
             dismantled. In the interest of occupational safety and health, the work shall be performed

in accordance with relevant IS codes on demolition and other applicable Sections. In the
        interest of conservation, salvage shall be pursued to the maximum extent possible. The
      salvaged items and materials shall be disposed of as specified in which the ‘owner losing
       structure totally/partially’ and the ‘contractor’ has no interest. The work also includes
       disconnection of power supply with the permission of BESCOM, rewiring and shifting of
      energy meter along with accessories to the suitable place as per BESCOM’s direction for
        partially demolished building. For full demolition of buildings, disconnection of power
       supply, releasing and handing over the electrical energy meter along with accessories as
       per directions of concerned BESCOM office through govt. licensed electrician.

    (c) Restoration works for safety reasons.
      The BMRCL has appointed consultant/Engineer who has conducted Building Condition
      Study (BCS) and suggest sequence and methodology of demolition including remedial
      measures required to be undertaken prior to demolition and / or during demolition and /
       or post demolition.

            It is anticipated that, certain structures will be required to be constructed for safety and
        functional reasons as a result of Building Condition Study. The structures anticipated
       are front walls, doors, windows, beams and columns etc.
      Works done as permanent remedial measures (for example –excavation, backfilling,
     PCC, RCC, brick/RR/CC block masonry, fixing of doors, windows, plastering, painting of
       face of wall remained after demolition, water supply, sanitation, electrical works including
       restoration of power supply to the balance building portion through govt. licensed
        electrician, etc.) shall be paid as per accepted price for the BoQ schedule for KPWD-
     Common SR 2023-24. The contractor shall carry out these works  after obtaining
        instructions from Consultant  / Engineer/BMRCL to that effect. The contractor has to
      execute these items in accordance with KPWD-Common SR 2023-24 and rate in the
      accepted priced bill of quantities. Measurements will be recorded for only those buildings
      completed under the supervision of consultant/Engineer appointed for Building Condition
       Study.

clauses.title: Work Plan
clauses.heading_line: 2.   Work Plan.   The procedures shall provide for safe conduct of the work, including

fragments.text:
2.   Work Plan.   The procedures shall provide for safe conduct of the work, including
     methods to provide necessary supports, lateral bracing and shoring when required, careful
      removal and disposition of materials to be salvaged, protection of property, which is to
      remain undisturbed, coordination with other work in progress, and timely disconnection of
         utility services. The procedures shall include a detailed description of methods and
      equipment to be used for each operation, and the sequence of operations.
     The contractor in addition to the proposed methodology should include the following:
           Initial Engineering survey of the building to be done.
         Developing strengthening methods of the balance portion of the structure not being
          dismantled and neighboring buildings.
         The actual method of dismantling proposed to be adopted.

clauses.title: Dust Control
clauses.heading_line: 3.    Dust Control. The dust resulting from demolition shall be controlled to prevent the spread

fragments.text:
3.    Dust Control. The dust resulting from demolition shall be controlled to prevent the spread
       of dust to occupied portions of the construction site and to avoid creation of a nuisance in
      the surrounding area. Use of water will not be permitted when it will result in, or create,
      hazardous or objectionable conditions such as flooding and pollution. The contractor shall
      take all measures to bring down dust level and cause least pollution in air quality and take
      necessary measures to keep the noise pollution as low as possible.

clauses.title: Protection of Personnel
clauses.heading_line: 4.    Protection of Personnel.    During  the   demolition  work   the   contractor   shall

fragments.text:
4.    Protection of Personnel.    During  the   demolition  work   the   contractor   shall
      continuously evaluate the condition of the structure being demolished and take immediate
      action to protect all people working in and around the demolition site. No area, section, or
     component of floors, roofs, walls, columns, pilasters, or other structural element will be
      allowed to be left standing without sufficient bracing, shoring, or lateral support to prevent

collapse or failure while workmen remove debris or perform other work in the immediate
             area. The contractor shall use wire nets etc., liberally so that falling debris etc., will not
           cause any  injury  to  people  in  the  premises. The methods  to be adopted  for
             dismantling/demolition of the structures should be apprised in advance to BMRCL.

clauses.title: Protection of Structures
clauses.heading_line: 5.    Protection of Structures.    Floors, roofs, walls, columns, pilasters, and other structural

fragments.text:
5.    Protection of Structures.    Floors, roofs, walls, columns, pilasters, and other structural
           components that are designed and constructed to stand without lateral support or shoring,
          and are determined to be in stable condition, shall remain standing without additional
             bracing, shoring, of lateral support until demolished, unless directed otherwise by the
             contracting officer.  The contractor shall ensure that no elements determined to be
            unstable are left unsupported and shall be responsible for placing and securing bracing,
             shoring, or lateral supports as may be required as a result of any cutting, removal, or
             demolition work performed under this contract.

clauses.title: Protection of Existing Property
clauses.heading_line: 6.    Protection of Existing Property.    Before  beginning  any  demolition  work,  the

fragments.text:
6.    Protection of Existing Property.    Before  beginning  any  demolition  work,  the
             contractor shall survey the site and examine the drawings and specifications to determine
            the extent of the work. The contractor shall take necessary precautions to avoid damage
              to existing items to remain in place, to be reused or to remain the property any damaged
            items shall be repaired or replaced as approved by the Engineer. The contractor shall
            coordinate the work of this section with all other work and shall construct and maintain that
              structural elements are not overloaded and shall be responsible for increasing structural
            supports or adding new supports as may be required as a result of any cutting, removal,
             or demolition work performed under this contract.

clauses.title: Protection from the weather
clauses.heading_line: 7.    Protection from the weather.      Salvageable  materials and equipment  shall be

fragments.text:
7.    Protection from the weather.      Salvageable  materials and equipment  shall be
             protected from the weather at all times.

clauses.title: Protection of Trees
clauses.heading_line: 8.    Protection of Trees.  Trees within the project sites which might be damaged during

fragments.text:
8.    Protection of Trees.  Trees within the project sites which might be damaged during
             demolition and which are indicated to be left in place shall be protected by a high fence.
          The fence shall be securely erected a minimum of 2 m from the trunk of individual trees
             or follow the outer perimeter of branches or clumps of trees. Any tree designated to remain
              that is damaged during the work under this contract shall be replaced in kind or as
           approved by the contracting officer.

clauses.title: Environmental Protection
clauses.heading_line: 9.    Environmental Protection.  The work shall comply with the requirements of relevant

fragments.text:
9.    Environmental Protection.  The work shall comply with the requirements of relevant
            environment protection clauses.

clauses.title: Burning
clauses.heading_line: 10.   Burning.      Burning at the project site for disposal of refuse and debris is not permitted.

fragments.text: 10.   Burning.      Burning at the project site for disposal of refuse and debris is not permitted.

clauses.heading_line: 11.   Use of explosives.  Use of explosives will not be permitted

fragments.text: 11.   Use of explosives.  Use of explosives will not be permitted

clauses.title: Utilities
clauses.heading_line: 12.    Utilities.       Existing utilities shall be removed as indicated. When utility lines are

fragments.text:
12.    Utilities.       Existing utilities shall be removed as indicated. When utility lines are
           encountered that is not indicated on the drawings, the contractor shall be notified prior to
              further work in that area, and shall follow instruction.

clauses.title: Filling
clauses.heading_line: 13.    Filling. Holes, open basements and  other hazardous openings  shall be  filled  in

fragments.text:
13.    Filling. Holes, open basements and  other hazardous openings  shall be  filled  in
           accordance with relevant IS codes.

clauses.title: Disposal of material
clauses.heading_line: 14.    Disposal of material. The Contractor shall dispose the demolished materials except

fragments.text:
14.    Disposal of material. The Contractor shall dispose the demolished materials except
           Government Salvage and historical items, which shall be duly informed to the Engineer
           and shall be handed over to the appropriate authorities as per the procedure in vogue.
           The rates quoted by the contractor includes loading, unloading and stacking with all lead
           and lifts to dispose the demolished materials.

clauses.title: Salvageable items and material
clauses.heading_line: 15.   Salvageable items and material. As per Compensation and Resettlement guidelines of

fragments.text:
15.   Salvageable items and material. As per Compensation and Resettlement guidelines of
     BMRCL, the owner losing land and structure has the right to salvage materials totally. In
       the case of items required by the ‘owner losing structure totally/partially’, he shall remove
       the same from the site before the contractor demobilizes from the site. The salvage
       materials in which the ‘owner losing structure totally/partially’ is not interested shall be
      owned by the Contractor and the value of the same shall be credited to BMRCL to the
     maximum extent possible.

clauses.title: Material Salvaged for the contractor
clauses.heading_line: 16.   Material Salvaged for the contractor.     The contractor shall not sell the salvaged

fragments.text:
16.   Material Salvaged for the contractor.     The contractor shall not sell the salvaged
      materials at site.

clauses.title: Item salvaged for the Government
clauses.heading_line: 17.   Item salvaged for the Government.        In the case of salvaged materials of the

fragments.text:
17.   Item salvaged for the Government.        In the case of salvaged materials of the
     Government, the contractor shall remove the salvaged materials in a manner that there is
     no damage while packing or carting and protect the materials from damage during storage
      or transportation. In case of any damage during storage or transportation, the same shall
     be repaired or replaced to match the existing items. Dismantled/released materials to be
     handed over to the concerned authorities at the locations specified by the owning
       authority.

clauses.title: Clean up
clauses.heading_line: 18.   Clean up.     Debris and rubbish shall be removed from basement, ground and any

fragments.text:
18.   Clean up.     Debris and rubbish shall be removed from basement, ground and any
      other stacking place. Debris shall be removed and transported in a manner that prevents
       spillage on streets or adjacent areas and no spillage is allowed during transportation.

clauses.title: Handing over of work front
clauses.heading_line: 19.   Handing over of work front. List  of  buildings  to be demolished  including area  of

fragments.text:
19.   Handing over of work front. List  of  buildings  to be demolished  including area  of
      demolition etc. will be made available to the contractor by BMRCL progressively.

clauses.title: Barricading the properties during demolition / dismantling
clauses.heading_line: 20.   Barricading the properties during demolition / dismantling.   The structure  to be

fragments.text:
20.   Barricading the properties during demolition / dismantling.   The structure  to be
      demolished/dismantled must have barricades, which shall be of plain MS Sheet of 16
     gauge fixed with steel frame, painting, with synthetic enamel paint of approved color,
       quality and brand, writing letter and logo of metro including maintenance of the same, duly
      cleaning the same frequently, arrangement for blinker light as per requirement. During
      demolition barricades has to be kept continuously. Removal of barricade will not be
      permitted till completion of demolition, dismantling of properties.

clauses.title: Demolition of buildings/structures
clauses.heading_line: 21.   Demolition of buildings/structures is to be done by ensuring minimal vibration, without

fragments.text:
21.   Demolition of buildings/structures is to be done by ensuring minimal vibration, without
       affecting the stability/serviceability of the remaining structure after demolition. Dismantling
       of structure is permitted only by using diamond disc cutter/floor saw machine at all levels.
     However, the decision of Engineer in charge is final and binding on the contractor. The
       structural integrity of the remaining structure  will be analyzed by structural experts
     engaged by Employer/Engineer by visual observation and necessary Non-Destructive
      Tests. In case any defect is noticed on account of demolition / dismantling activity and/or
     any claim is raised by the owner of the building/structure, the damage will be repaired and
       claim, if any, shall be settled by the contractor, failing which the defects will be rectified at
      the risk and cost of the contractor as per the directions of Engineer/Employer and the
     same will be recovered from the contractor. Necessary scaffolding to be provided to
        facilitate the dismantling of buildings/structures as mentioned in the line-of-cut proposed
     by structural experts or as directed by the Engineer In-charge. The scaffolding shall have
       to be erected with proper anchors to ensure safety &  stability during demolition  /
      dismantling.
